metadata.title: Arm falls 10% as modest revenue outlook fails to impress investors

content.text:
Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM) shares fell 10% to $172.01 on Thursday after quarterly results beat estimates, but revenue guidance landed just above analysts' forecasts.
The British semiconductor technology company reported fiscal second-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share against estimates of $0.47, with revenue of $1.44 billion topping the $1.38 billion consensus.
For the third quarter, Arm forecast adjusted earnings of $0.56 per share, plus or minus $0.04, compared with analysts' expectations of $0.55.
Its revenue outlook similarly offered a modest premium to expectations, with a midpoint of $1.54 billion against the $1.53 billion consensus.
The revenue forecast carries a $50 million allowance in either direction, putting the range at $1.49 billion to $1.59 billion.
In the reported quarter, revenue grew 27% from a year earlier, including a 50% increase in license and other revenue to $773 million.
Arm's royalty revenue grew more slowly, rising 8% to $670 million as gains from higher rates and increased data-center deployment were partly offset by memory pricing's impact on smartphones.
The company also reported adjusted operating income of $638 million, representing an adjusted operating margin of 44%.
